name: Basilica of St. Joseph Proto-Cathedral
history: The Diocese of Bardstown, created in 1808, was the first inland diocese in the United States. Its cathedral's cornerstone was laid on 16 July 1816, with materials from the local area, and Mass was held in it by 1819 under Bishop Benedict Joseph Flaget. When the see moved to Louisville, St. Joseph became the "proto-cathedral". It is the first Catholic cathedral west of the Allegheny Mountains and became a basilica in 2001.
arch: A brick church with a columned portico and a steeple, built by John Rogers of Baltimore. It was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1974.
features: It keeps a painting given by King Francis I of the Two Sicilies in the early 1800s.
An umbraculum, the basilica's canopy, was installed at the altar in 2001.

look.d: Classical columns at the front of the first cathedral west of the Alleghenies.
The steeple has watched over Bardstown since the early 1800s.

fun: "Proto-cathedral" means the first cathedral of a diocese that has since moved its seat.
journal: The first cathedral west of the mountains, in bourbon country. Built with local materials.

a: The original cathedral of a see that moved
